This should be
```suggestion
	const String mirrors_metadata_url = vformat("https://godotengine.org/mirrorlist/%s.json", GODOT_VERSION_FULL_CONFIG);
```
However dev builds have no available mirrors, so I left this option for testing.

This allows testing the PR using locally hosted templates. The easiest way is to run `python -m http.server` inside templates directory from some offical release.

DO NOT use the official mirror, it downloads the whole template package for each file xd
I suppose this could be an editor setting 🤔

I'm considering replacing the Dictionary metadata with a struct. Instead of using the TreeItem metadata, there'd be a HashMap of <String, MetadataStruct>. It's better for performance and type safety, although it's not some crucial improvement.

I added translations for some templates (that are more than just platform name), but it's rather arbitrary, so not sure if it's ok. However translating all template names makes no sense either.

Kinda wish the logic for updating the translations wasn't as awkward (some entries have duplicate definitions). Maybe I should just clear the data and re-run the initialize method when language changes.

`"User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0"` 

https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Reference/Headers/User-Agent

We can also remove this header to save data traffic, or we can pass `Godot Engine {version}` there.
This would need to either check module support or add it to the required editor modules I'd say

For this PR yes, it can be made a required editor module.

Going further we should consider whether this should have been a module in the first place, that's how it was contributed but I assume it has a small impact on binary size and could be in `core/io`.
There is actually some `core/io/zip_io.cpp` file, the ZIPReader seems to be a higher-level API. I could replace it with the core one.
I used Wikipedia as reference, but ok.
This new behavior should be documented in the TreeItem class reference.
